authors: E. W. Tiepel, K. E. Gubbins
title: Partial molal volumes of gases dissolved in electrolyte solutions
needs_pass2_reason: text layer for Table I was scrambled (columns scattered) but table was read completely from the 300 dpi image, clear print; no cell corrections of a text-layer CSV were needed (CSV built from image)
experimental_method: Horiuti dilatometer: volume change on addition of known gas amounts to degassed solution at 25 C, partial molal volume from slope of volume change vs moles of gas.
uncertainties_stated: estimated accuracy +-3 percent in water, up to +-6 percent in electrolyte solutions; table gives standard deviation of the mean of three or more experiments
quality_remarks: Main error source temperature fluctuations. Gas purities 99.9% (Ar, H2, O2) and 99.0% (CH4, C2H6). Table II (comparison with literature and calculated values) not extracted. Molarity basis not defined.

not_extracted_tables.reason: water-only comparison of this work with literature values and theory-calculated (Eq 14, Lyckman) values; derived/model values

extraction_notes: Blank gas cells of continuation rows filled down. +- split into two columns. Sanity: V1 decreases with salt molarity for KCl, KI, CaCl2, KOH and increases for R4NBr, as the paper states.
pass2_diff: Table I: all measured numbers identical; the pass-1-only numbers are the digits of gas names (O2, N2) filled down where pass 2 left them blank.
